title: deskcrit report
description: The JSON document that crit report --json writes (docs/PRD.md section 8.1, FR-26, FR-31, FR-33). Written for JSON Schema draft 2020-12; the $schema keyword is left out by project rule, so a validator must be set to draft 2020-12. Every object rejects unknown fields, because the schema and the CLI ship together: a new optional field is added here in the same change that adds it to the output.

schema_version.description: The version of this output shape, as a semantic version (section 8).

mode.description: Always report for this document. The gate document reuses the $defs with mode gate (section 8.3).

model.description: The versioned model id from the response (FR-33).

semantic_version.description: A semantic version string, for example 1.0.0, with optional pre-release and build parts (https://semver.org).

tool.description: The name and version of the tool that wrote the document.

image.description: The image that was judged: its path and size. padded is present, and true, only when prepare padded the image (FR-8).

context.description: The optional context the run used (FR-2). Each key is optional.

pack.description: One pack the run used, by name and version.

finding.description: One judged criterion (FR-26). All ten fields are present on every finding, whatever its verdict.

criterion.description: Pack name and criterion id joined by /. The pack schema sets the allowed characters.

distribution.description: Jev's probability for each option or level, keyed by option name or level index, unchanged and unrounded.

confidence.description: Jev's confidence in the distribution, from 0 to 1, as TypeSafe reports it. Null for a noul finding (FR-20, FR-26).

region.description: Where on the original image, from a Box question, or null.

link.description: The URL of the source when it is online, or null.

region.description: A rectangle in pixels of the original image.

skipped_entry.description: A criterion that was not asked, and why.

usage.description: What the run cost (FR-33). The model id is in the top-level model field and on each finding, never here.
